note — the bold part is what the card te: ich: the stem wohn- (the infinitive minus -en) plus -e.
du: the stem plus -st.
er, sie and es: the stem plus -t.
wir: the stem plus -en, the same as the infinitive. German has one present for both we learn and we are learning.
ihr: the stem plus -t, the same ending as er.
sie (they) takes -en, like wir.
Formal Sie takes -en, like wir and they.
ich: arbeit- plus -e.
The stem ends in -t, so an extra e goes before -st to make it sayable: arbeitest.
After a stem in -t, er takes -et: arbeitet. German uses the present for plans too.
ihr also needs the extra e after the t: arbeitet.
trink- plus -t. Kaffee has no article here, as in English.
trink- plus -e.
A noun subject takes the er ending: -t.
die Katze is one subject, so trinkt, like sie.
wir kaufen; the object der Tisch becomes einen Tisch.
kauf- plus -t; sie with -t means she, not they.
koch- plus -st.
koch- plus -t. oft comes after the verb, not before it as in English.
hören takes its object directly: no word for to.
wir hören; oft follows the verb.
German says I play gladly: gern after the verb means you like doing it.
wir kochen + gern: we like to cook.
The verb stays the main verb; gern only adds the liking.
komm- plus -st.
wir gehen: the -en form, the same as the infinitive.
komm- plus -t.
machen covers both make and do.
lern- plus -t.
geh- plus -e.
heute takes the first place, so the verb stays second and ich moves after it.
Only one thing goes before the verb: morgen, then the verb, then wir.
jetzt first, verb second, then the subject er.
English keeps she before the verb; German puts the verb second and sie after it.
A noun subject also moves behind the verb: kommt die Frau.
hier can open the sentence too; then the verb comes second and wir follows.
Any verb keeps the second place: heute, habe, ich.
heute first, ist second, das Kind third.

English: I am working today, but tomorrow I **have** time.
German: Ich arbeite heute, aber morgen **habe** ich Zeit.
note — the bold part is what the card te: aber stands outside the count; morgen is first, so habe comes second.

English: We play football often, and today we **are playing** too.
German: Wir spielen oft Fußball, und heute **spielen** wir auch.
note — the bold part is what the card te: und does not count as a position: heute is first, spielen second.
